title: A Module Call Within the Host
statement: Let $M_0,\ldots,M_4$ be five finite Boolean Turing machines, let $K$ bound each machine's number of work tapes, and fix a module $i$ with $0<(M_i).k$. Suppose that, on input $x$ with argument word $\mathrm{arg}$ on tape zero, machine $M_i$ starts in its initial state, does not halt at any time $v<t$, and at time $t$ is halted with result word $\mathrm{result}$ on tape zero and output $\mathrm{out}$. Then the host started at module $i$'s entry with the same argument and output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$ does not reach the loop anchor at any time $v<t$; at time $t$ it is in module $i$'s resolved return state, with result word on tape zero and output $\mathrm{pre}$ followed by $\mathrm{out}$.
hypotheses_covered: Five Boolean finite Turing machines indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(5)$
A shared tape bound $K$ with $(M_j).k\le K$ for every $j$
The module run does not halt at any time $v<t$
At time $t$ the module run equals the halted canonical configuration with state $q$, tape word $\mathrm{result}$, and output $\mathrm{out}$
replaced: Suppose a module runs from its start over an argument word to a halted canonical seam with a result word and output chunk in time $t$, never halting earlier. Then the host, started at that module's entry over the shared bank with an output prefix, never shows the loop anchor before $t$, and at $t$ sits at the module's resolved return over the result word with the output prefix extended by exactly the module's chunk.
